page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The system is driven by 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The compute architecture allocates high memory density relative to core count, delivering a total of 32.0 GB of RAM at an allocation rate of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance relies exclusively on network-attached storage, as zero local disk capacity is bundled. In addition, no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs are included. Network connectivity is configured with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual private cloud routing or assigned elastic IP addresses for external traffic.

Because the platform emphasizes an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it provides qualitative cost efficiency for software bounded by memory constraints rather than CPU throughput. The absence of local disk drives requires external block storage, which isolates data persistence from the compute instance at the expense of local bus I/O performance. The ecs.r9i.xlarge configuration is suited for operational workloads such as in-memory caches, distributed databases, ETL pipelines, and stateful application services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed using the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at 3.2 GHz, backed by 32.0 GB of system memory. This yields a memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, targeting workloads that require significant memory arrays without excessive core overhead. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and standard network routing over a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Due to its dedicated processor allotment and memory-to-vCPU balance, the ecs.r9i.xlarge is structurally suited for memory-bound tasks including in-memory datastores, relational databases, backend caching layers, and enterprise memory-intensive data processing.
